title: Blackwood Manor
intro: Lord Ashworth was found slumped in his armchair at midnight. The doors were locked from the inside. One of the four people in this house is a murderer. Explore the manor, scan what you find, question the suspects, then make your accusation.

library.name: The Library
library.desc: Floor-to-ceiling shelves, a dying fire, and the smell of old paper. A chair is pulled out as though someone left in a hurry.

kitchen.name: The Kitchen
kitchen.desc: Copper pans hang over a scrubbed table. A tea tray sits half-prepared by the stove.

greenhouse.name: The Greenhouse
greenhouse.desc: Warm, damp and overgrown. Tall purple flowers crowd one bench; the soil there has been freshly disturbed.

cellar.name: The Wine Cellar
cellar.desc: Cold air and rows of dusty racks. Many of the shelves are strangely empty.
cellar.locked: The cellar door is bolted shut with a heavy brass lock. There is no way through without a key. Somebody in this house must keep one...

niece.name: Vivian Ashworth
niece.statement: I was in the library all evening. Uncle and I argued at supper, yes, but I never touched his tea.

cook.name: Mrs. Penhallow
cook.statement: I cleared the kitchen at ten and went straight to bed. Anyone in this house could have touched that tea tray.

gardener.name: Mr. Thorne
gardener.statement: Repotting in the greenhouse until midnight, I was. I know every plant in it, and I would never harm a living soul.

butler.name: Henry Crane
butler.statement: I was down in the cellar rotating the stock. His Lordship was perfectly well when I last saw him at nine.

torn-letter.name: A torn letter
torn-letter.text: A letter in Lord Ashworth’s hand, torn in half: “...I have proof that someone in this household has been selling my cellar and pocketing the money. On Friday I will change my will and call in the auditors...”

ledger.name: The cellar ledger
ledger.text: Forty-one vintages written off as “spoiled” this year. Every write-off was countersigned by whoever holds the cellar keys.

cellar-key.name: A brass key
cellar-key.text: A brass key tagged CELLAR – SPARE. A note in Lord Ashworth’s writing is tied to it: “The other is kept by the butler.”

teacup.name: His Lordship’s teacup
teacup.text: The dregs smell faintly bitter. Foxglove. Someone put digitalis in the tea.

gloves.name: A pair of leather gloves
gloves.text: Far too fine for gardening, and stained green with foxglove sap. Inside the cuff is a monogram: H.C.

codicil.name: An unsigned codicil
codicil.text: Hidden behind a loose crate: Ashworth’s new will. It dismisses the butler without pension and orders a full audit of the cellar. It was never signed.
